title: Joining a round — sl st join vs invisible join
subtitle: Two ways to close a round without a visible seam
excerpt: Crochet rounds are closed with a slip stitch into the first stitch of the round. The standard slip stitch join leaves a small visible join line; the invisible join method uses a tapestry needle and yarn to mimic the top of the stitch, hiding the join completely. Both have their place depending on whether the join will show.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of closing a crochet round by cutting the yarn and threading the tail through the last stitch top, then under both loops of the first stitch and back under the last stitch — mimicking the V of a normal stitch top. No slip stitch needed; the join disappears into the fabric.

content.text: At the end of each round, a join closes the circle and steps up to the next round. The standard method is a
into the first stitch of the round. The
is used when the round ends the piece — usually the final round of a granny square or flat motif where the join line would otherwise be seen.
Complete the last stitch of the round.
Insert hook into both loops of the first stitch of the round (not the turning chain).
Yarn over and pull through the stitch and the loop on the hook in one motion — slip stitch made. Round joined.
Complete the last stitch of the round. Cut yarn, leaving a 15 cm tail. Pull the tail through the last stitch loop to secure.
Thread the tail onto a tapestry needle. Insert the needle under both loops of the first stitch of the round from the top.
Insert the needle back into the top of the last stitch — under both loops from the outside — and pull the tail through.
Pull gently to tension the join to match the surrounding stitches. Weave in the tail.

items.symptom: Join still visible after invisible join
items.cause: Tail pulled too tight or left too loose — the mimic stitch doesn't match the tension of real stitches
items.fix: Match the tension of the surrounding stitches by eye before weaving in. The fake stitch top should sit at the same height as the real stitches.

content.text: Continuous spiral rounds (no joining, no turning) avoid the join altogether — common in amigurumi where the join stitch would interrupt the smooth surface of the piece. Use a stitch marker in the first stitch of each round to track position.
